The short pulse width confines energy deposition and minimizes heat-affected zone damage to the underlying fibers, and the resulting texture conforms to the woven laminate (warp/weft).Mechanistically,thegroovesproviderapid capillarydrainageand pin the three-phase contact line, whereas the polygonal cels increase the real contact area, together enhancing wet adhesion and friction on wet substrates.

All characterization and measurement procedures were conducted using a range of advanced analytical instruments to ensure the comprehensive evaluation of the samples. The surface morphology and three-dimensional topography were observed using a laser confocal microscope (DCM8, Leica), with an X-Y lateral resolution of noless than 0.14m and a Z(height) resolution of up to 0.1nm.A contactangle goniometer(LSA 100) measuredthe contact angle to assess surface wettability. An x-ray photoelectron spectrometer (XPS, ESCALAB Xi+, Thermo Fisher Scientific) analyzedsurface chemical composition after laseractivation,whilea Raman spectrometer (Renishaw inVia Qontor) identified structural changes and chemical composition.
